content: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms. It focuses on understanding the characteristics, classification, and behaviors of organisms, the processes by which species originate, and the interactions they have with one another and their environment. The field of biology spans a wide range of disciplines, each addressing specific phenomena related to living organisms, from molecular biology to ecology. All biological concepts adhere to universal scientific laws, such as the laws of thermodynamics and the conservation of energy. The Essence of Biology Biology encompasses the study of anatomy, human anatomy, the concept of life, and the structure and function of organisms. Subdisciplines of Biology Biology is divided into various subfields, each focusing on specific aspects of life and living systems. History of Biology The history of biology includes contributions from ancient Greek medicine, Islamic medicine, Byzantine medicine, and medieval medicine. It also covers the history of anatomy, plant systematics, evolutionary thought, natural history, genetics, model organisms, biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, and molecular evolution. The modern evolutionary synthesis is a key milestone in the field. Basic Biology Concepts Ecology and Evolution Origin of Life: Theories and experiments, such as the Miller-Urey experiment, explore the origin of life. Ecology: Includes autecology (study of individual species), autotrophs, heterotrophs, acclimatization, endotherms, ectotherms, hibernation, homeostasis, behavior, and circadian rhythms. Population Ecology: Examines populations, competition, mating, biological dispersal, endemism, niches, growth curves, and carrying capacity. Community Ecology: Studies communities, keystone species, mimicry, symbiosis, pollination, mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, invasive species, environmental heterogeneity, and edge effects. Ecosystems: Focuses on biodiversity, biomes, habitats, plankton, thermoclines, carbon cycle, water cycle, nitrogen cycle, food webs, trophic levels, saprobes, and decomposition. Evolutionary Biology Microevolution: Includes species, speciation, adaptation, selection, natural selection, directional selection, sexual selection, genetic drift, sexual and asexual reproduction, colonies, allele frequency, neutral theory of molecular evolution, population genetics, and the Hardy-Weinberg principle. Macroevolution: Covers adaptive radiation, convergent evolution, extinction, mass extinction, fossils, taphonomy, geologic time, plate tectonics, continental drift, vicariance, Gondwana, Pangaea, and endosymbiosis. Systematics: Involves taxonomy, scientific classification, phylogeny, evolutionary trees, cladistics, synapomorphy, homology, and molecular clocks. Organismal Biology Groups of Living Organisms Viruses: DNA viruses, RNA viruses, and retroviruses. Single-Celled Organisms: Prokaryotes (microbes, bacteria, archaebacteria, eubacteria) and eukaryotes (fungi, algae, protozoa, protists). Multicellular Organisms: Plantae (plants, bryophytes, pteridophytes, seed plants), Animalia (animals, metazoa, insects, mollusks, vertebrates), and fungi (lichens, mycorrhizae). Developmental Biology Animal Development: Includes gametes (spermatids, ova), zygotes, embryos, cellular differentiation, morphogenesis, homeobox genes, stem cells, blastula, gastrula, eggs, fetuses, and placenta. Plant Development: Covers seeds, cotyledons, meristems, apical meristems, vascular cambium, and cork cambium. Morphology, Anatomy, and Physiology Techniques: Electrophysiology and electron microscopy. Plant Systems: Roots, shoots, stems, leaves, flowers, vascular tissues (xylem, phloem), Casparian strip, turgor pressure, transpiration, wood, alternation of generations, gametophytes, antheridia, archegonia, sporophytes, spores, sporangia, tropism, and taxis. Animal Systems: Skin cells, skeleton (bones, cartilage, joints), muscles (actin, myosin, tendons), reflexes, circulatory system (lungs, heart, arteries, veins, capillaries, blood, blood cells), digestive system (stomach, intestines, liver, nutrition, metabolism, kidneys, excretion), nervous system (limbic system, vestibular system, neurons, axons, dendrites, brain, eyes, vision, audition, proprioception, olfaction, memory), nerve signaling (action potentials, signal transduction, synapses, receptors), endocrine system (hormones), and reproductive system (testes, ovaries, pregnancy). Cell and Molecular Biology Cell Biology Techniques: Cell culture, microscopy (SEM, TEM). Cell Components: Organelles (Golgi apparatus, nucleus, cytoplasm, vacuoles, vesicles, lysosomes, peroxisomes, mitochondria, plastids, chloroplasts), membranes (plasma membrane, endomembrane system, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondrial membrane, chloroplast membrane), and other subcellular features (cell wall, pseudopodia, cytoskeleton, mitotic spindle, flagella, cilia). Cell Processes: Diffusion, osmosis, isotonicity, active transport, phagocytosis, energy pathways (fermentation, glycolysis, cellular respiration, citric acid cycle, photosynthesis, Calvin cycle), protein biosynthesis (ribosomes), cellular reproduction (cytokinesis, centromeres, meiosis), nuclear reproduction (mitosis, interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase), programmed cell death (apoptosis, cell senescence). Biochemistry Biomolecules: Small molecules (amino acids, ATP, fats, lipids, oils, phospholipids, prions, sugars, vitamins, neurotransmitters, waxes), medium-sized molecules (pigments like chlorophyll, carotenoids, xanthophylls, melanin), and biopolymers/macromolecules (proteins, DNA, RNA, polysaccharides like cellulose, carbohydrates, chitin, glycogen, starch). Biochemical Mechanisms: Proteolysis, cooperativity. Techniques: Electrophoresis, His-tag, affinity chromatography, x-ray diffraction, proteomics, mass spectrometry. Molecular Biology Genetic Structure: DNA, DNA replication, nucleosomes, genetic code, codons, transcription factors, transcription, translation, RNA, histones, telomeres. Gene Expression: Heterochromatin, promoters, enhancers, operons. Mutations: Point mutations, crossover, recombination, plasmids, transposons. Molecular Genetics: DNA fingerprinting, genetic fingerprints, microsatellites, gene knockouts, imprinting, RNA interference. Genomics: Computational biology, bioinformatics. Molecular Techniques: Gel electrophoresis, transformation, PCR, PCR mutagenesis, primers, chromosome walking, RFLP, restriction enzymes, sequencing, shotgun sequencing, cloning, DNA microarrays. Genetics (Classical Genetics) Heredity: Mendelian inheritance, genes, loci, traits, alleles, polymorphisms, homozygotes, heterozygotes, hybrids, hybridization, dihybrid crosses, Punnett squares. Genotype-Phenotype Distinction: Genotypes, phenotypes, dominant and recessive genes. Genetic Interactions: Mendel's law of segregation, genetic mosaics, maternal effects, penetrance, complementation, suppression, epistasis, genetic linkage. Chromosomal Effects: Chromosomes, haploidy, diploidy, polyploidy, dosage effects, inbreeding. Model Organisms: Drosophila, Arabidopsis, Caenorhabditis elegans, mice, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Escherichia coli, lambda phage, Xenopus. Techniques: Genetic screens, paternity tests, linkage maps, genetic maps. Influential Biologists Key figures in biology include Charles Darwin, Alfred Russel Wallace, Jean-Baptiste Lamarck, Sir Charles Lyell, Alfred Wegener, Alexander Fleming, Andrew Huxley, Robert Koch, Konrad Lorenz, Ernst Haeckel, Theodor Bilharz, Marcello Malpighi, Antoni van Leeuwenhoek, Thomas Malthus, Edward Jenner, Carolus Linnaeus, Sewall Wright, Louis Pasteur, Gregor Mendel, Barbara McClintock, James Watson, Francis Crick, Kary Mullis, Rosalind Franklin, Steven Jay Gould, Lynn Margulis, Carl Woese, and Jane Goodall.
